- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction, dampening forecast by 10–20% in following days.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at 10–15% above recent high.
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.8 to 0.1), model reacts too quickly; delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and smooth transition.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently below forecast (e.g., 5–10% gap), apply downward bias of 1–3% per day for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is negative and price is falling, model often underestimates; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast to avoid under-shock.
